correctness.rationale: Each leaf v_i is the unique vertex separating u_i from edge u_i v_i, so every mixed resolving set contains all leaves. Direct formulas show the leaf set resolves every vertex and edge. It does not dominate the center, forcing one extra vertex; adding c or any u_i is sufficient, and no other extra vertex exists outside the leaf set. Exhaustive verification for q=3,...,8 matches the theorem.

value.rationale: Once-subdivided stars form the minimal uniform subdivision of the star family already treated in the introducing paper. The subdivision creates a sharp structural transition: the forced leaf mixed basis stops dominating the center, causing an exact +1 increase and exactly q+1 minimum repairs. This gives a natural boundary case for dominant mixed metric dimension on spiders rather than a mere recomputation of ordinary mixed dimension.
